```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 110)
library(sciparseR)
```

A parser should be judged by measurement, not by its own description.
`sc_evaluate()` compares a parsed document with a ground truth file and
reports standard measures.

## The fixtures

Nine synthetic PDF files are generated by `data-raw/make-fixtures.R` with
known content. Each targets a failure mode: two columns, a scrambled
content stream, running headers and hyphenation, spanning table headers,
missing values, a rotated page, an image-only page, Unicode symbols, a
figure, an equation and a table continued across pages. Each comes with a
`.truth.json` file that lists blocks in reading order, sections and the
expected cell grid of every table.

```{r}
dir <- system.file("extdata", package = "sciparseR")
pdfs <- list.files(dir, pattern = "\\.pdf$")
pdfs <- pdfs[file.exists(file.path(dir, sub("\\.pdf$", ".truth.json", pdfs)))]
pdfs
```

## Measures

* `block_recall`: share of truth blocks (paragraphs, headings, captions,
  footnotes) found with normalized similarity above `threshold`. Matching
  is one to one in document order: a parsed block serves at most one
  truth block, and candidates share a 30 character anchor (start, middle
  or end) with the truth text.
* `reading_order_tau` and `reading_order_pairs`: Kendall's tau between
  truth order and parsed order, and the share of block pairs in the
  correct order.
* `section_precision`, `section_recall`, `section_f1` on heading titles.
* `character_error_rate`: Levenshtein edits between each truth block and
  its matched parsed block, over all truth characters; an unmatched truth
  block counts in full.
* `table_recall`, `table_structure` (rows and columns), `table_header_rows`,
  `table_cell_accuracy`, `table_spans` (row and column spans).
* `table_detection_precision` and `table_detection_recall` at area IoU 0.5
  on the same page, for truth tables with a full box (`x0`, `x1`, `top`,
  `bottom`). Truth tables with only `top` and `bottom` are scored on the
  IoU of the vertical extent and reported as
  `table_detection_precision_vertical` and `table_detection_recall_vertical`;
  the bundled fixtures are of this kind.
* `table_grits_con`: GriTS-Con (Smock et al. 2023) with the factored row
  and column alignment, on grids with spanned text in every covered
  position. The cell similarity follows the reference implementation in
  Microsoft's Table Transformer: matching blocks of Python's
  `difflib.SequenceMatcher`, reproduced exactly including its junk
  heuristic, on text with whitespace normalized and case kept.
* `table_teds`: TEDS (Zhong et al. 2020), one minus the tree edit
  distance (Zhang and Shasha) between the HTML-like trees of the two
  tables, divided by the number of nodes below the table node of the
  larger tree, as in the PubTabNet reference. Cell text keeps its case.
  Inline formatting (bold, italic, sub- and superscripts) is not part of
  the tree, so TEDS here equals the reference only for plain text cells.
* Ratios of found to expected figures, equations and references, DOI
  recall, image-only page detection.

```{r}
res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pdfs, function(f) {
  e <- sc_evaluate(sc_parse(file.path(dir, f)), file.path(dir, sub("\\.pdf$", ".truth.json", f)))
  data.frame(file = f, e)
}))
wide <- reshape(res[, c("file", "metric", "value")], idvar = "file", timevar = "metric", direction = "wide")
names(wide) <- sub("^value\\.", "", names(wide))
wide[, c("file", "block_recall", "character_error_rate", "reading_order_pairs", "section_f1",
         "table_cell_accuracy", "table_grits_con", "table_teds")]
```

The per table detail is an attribute:

```{r}
e <- sc_evaluate(sc_parse(file.path(dir, "trial_tables.pdf")), file.path(dir, "trial_tables.truth.json"))
attr(e, "tables")
```

## What these numbers mean

Perfect scores on the fixtures show that each component works on the case
it was built for. They do not show performance on real articles, whose
layouts are far more varied. A benchmark on real open access articles,
with their JATS version as the reference, and a comparison with GROBID,
Docling and Marker are planned for a later version; none of them was run
for this release.

## Extraction accuracy

The truth file of `trial_tables.pdf` also lists the 61 values the fixture
generator wrote into the text and tables, each with the context a careful
reader binds to it. `sc_evaluate_extraction()` matches extracted values
to them and scores the bindings. The main metrics count only accepted
values (status `reported`, not invalidated); the `candidate_` metrics count
every extracted value, so the two together show what review would remove.
Every context field a truth entry gives is scored, including population,
unit, adjustment, interval level and p-value operator, and an empty
context never counts as right:

```{r}
x <- sc_extract(sc_parse(file.path(dir, "trial_tables.pdf")), "clinical_trial")
sc_evaluate_extraction(x, file.path(dir, "trial_tables.truth.json"))
```

## Time and memory

`sc_benchmark()` parses each file a few times and reports the median
time and the growth of the R heap:

```{r}
sc_benchmark(file.path(dir, c("two_column.pdf", "trial_tables.pdf")), times = 2)
```

## Evaluating your own documents

Write a truth file in the same format for a document you care about and
pass it to `sc_evaluate()`; a list with the same structure works too:

```{r}
truth <- list(
  blocks = list(list(type = "heading", text = "Methods"),
                list(type = "heading", text = "Results")),
  sections = list(list(title = "Methods"), list(title = "Results")),
  tables = list(list(label = "Table 2", page = 1, header_rows = 1,
                     cells = list(list("Outcome", "Drug A", "Placebo", "HR (95% CI)", "P"))))
)
sc_evaluate(sc_parse(file.path(dir, "trial_tables.pdf")), truth)
```
